public_rationale: The claim is read as a description of AI in calendar 2025. Marcus qualified it with 'at least for now'. Two 2025 preprints fit it. The Remote Labor Index (Oct 2025) tests agents on real-world projects designed to measure end-to-end performance. The best agent reached an automation rate of 2.5% (e1). So AI often did not complete whole projects. GDPval (Oct 2025) builds tasks from the work of professionals averaging 14 years' experience (e3). On its 220-task gold subset, 47.6% of deliverables from Claude Opus 4.1, the best model there, were graded as better than or as good as the human expert's deliverable (e2). The other deliverables were graded worse than the human's. So AI did a real share of the work at expert quality, but not most of it. Neither study shows AI routinely completing whole jobs or matching experts on nearly all tasks. That is the contract's test for contradiction.
limitations: The benchmarks measure tasks and projects, not junior or senior job titles, and they do not measure judgement directly.
Calling a 47.6% match rate 'often lacks' is a matter of degree. The GDPval text also says models matched or beat experts on 'just over half' of tasks, which differs slightly from the 47.6% figure.
Both studies were published after the post, though they test models from 2025.
The result covers 2025 only. It says nothing about later models.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: in 2025, AI systems could do a real share of workplace tasks, but often could not complete whole jobs or projects end to end, and often fell short of experienced professionals' quality or judgment.
The period is the state of AI around the post, read as calendar 2025. Capability tests of the models available then were published in September–October 2025.
criteria.support_condition: 2025 evaluations show AI matching humans on a meaningful share of tasks, while failing on many whole projects or falling short of experts on a large share of tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: 2025 evaluations show AI routinely completing whole junior roles end to end and matching senior professionals on nearly all tasks, or doing almost none of the work.
